newsitem.title: UK: BA says report strengthens case for alliance.
newsitem.headline: BA says report strengthens case for alliance.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Wednesday a report that rivals were planning to strengthen their ties to create a single global network served only to strengthen the case for its proposed deal with American Airlines.

Airline industry sources told Reuters earlier that nine major carriers were planning to form a powerful new global alliance to counter the threat posed by the proposed link-up between BA and American.
The report said the grouping would build around the core alliance between United Airlines, Lufthansa and SAS.

But BA has always cited the Lufthansa-United-SAS axis, which already has the immunity from US anti-trust laws being sought by BA and American for their own deal, as being one of the main reasons why it should be allowed to link up with American.
"This report simply underlines the moves within the aviation industry to develop global networks for the benefit of customers," a spokesman for British Airways said.

"Our proposed alliance with American is a competitive response to those alliances already in place between U.S. and European carriers and what this report does underline quite firmly is the need for an agreement between BA and American to offer passengers a competitive alternative."

A manager with Air Canada, another partner with United and Lufthansa, had told Reuters earlier that plans are now afoot for that alliance to weave together a single global network using links with a number of other airlines.
Airlines mentioned included Thai International, Brazil's Varig, All Nippon Airways, South African Airways and British Midnland.
But BA did not see any new threat. "Everybody mentioned in this report already has agreements with one another in some shape or form," a spokesman said.
